Dear Shareholders,
The year under review, 2025-26, was 
marked by significant shifts in the 
global technology, economic and 
geopolitical landscape. Advances in 
Artificial Intelligence (AI) continued to 
drive innovation and transformation 
across industries, while the shifting 
global tariff regimes and the 
conflict in West Asia have disrupted 
supply chains, energy markets and 
capital flows.
Amidst this evolving environment, 
the Indian economy remained 
resilient. Increased public investment 
in infrastructure and initiatives 
promoting Aatmanirbharta (self-
reliance) reinforced India’s position as 
the fastest-growing major economy. As 
a management, we are trying our best 
to get mentally used to events beyond 
our comprehension and lookout − like 
the COVID-19 pandemic, Suez Canal 
blockage, Red Sea challenge, tariffs, 
unnatural price increase, conflict in 
West Asia, to name a few.
For Larsen & Toubro, 2025-26 was a 
year of steady progress. Record order 
inflows, strong revenue growth and 
improved profitability strengthened 
your Company’s presence across 
construction and infrastructure, hi-tech 
manufacturing and technology-driven 
services, while its continued focus on 
emerging sectors remained aligned 
with long-term strategic priorities.
The evolving situation in West Asia 
creates some near-term uncertainty. 
As a strategically important market for 
Larsen & Toubro, the developments in 
the region are being closely monitored 
by the management, with priority 
accorded to employee safety, business 
continuity and asset protection. Over 
time, the restoration of normalcy may 
also create opportunities for rebuilding 
and investment activity. 
Backed by nearly nine decades of 
experience in navigating external 
challenges, your Company remains 
confident, resilient and focused on 
delivering stable and consistent 
performance.
CHAIRMAN AND
MANAGING DIRECTOR
S. N. Subrahmanyan

Safety first
Workplace safety is of paramount 
importance. Your Company has 
evolved from its ‘Mission Zero Harm’ 
safety philosophy to a more proactive 
‘Vision Know Harm’ (phonetically 
‘Vision - No Harm’). While ‘Zero Harm’ 
(i.e. no loss of life or serious injuries) 
remains the ultimate goal, ‘Know 
Harm’ strategy strives to sensitise 
employees and workers in spotting 
risks in advance and empowers them 
to take corrective action. Extensive 
use of digital technologies is made to 
monitor safety lapses, detect high-risk 
activities and issue alerts real-time. As 
a result of these, during the year your 
Company has clocked 1,369 million 
accident-free working hours. 
To make occupational health and 
safety integral to its operations, 
the Company has institutionalised 
a structured Reward and Penalty 
mechanism for select EPC businesses. 
Under this framework, pre-defined 
EHS performance targets are linked to 
financial incentives and disincentives 
at the business unit level. Performance 
against these targets has a direct 
bearing on performance-linked pay 
outcomes for employees within the 
respective units, thereby strengthening 
accountability and oversight for safety 
performance.
(A) Infrastructure
The continued pursuit for quality and 
timely completion while executing 
large-scale, complex EPC projects has 
always been the hallmark of your 
Company. 
Highlights of the year:
• Kartavya Bhavan 1, 2 & 3 and Seva 
Teerth in Delhi inaugurated by 
Prime Minister of India 
• Phase 1 of the Navi Mumbai 
International Airport in 
Maharashtra inaugurated by Prime 
Minister of India
• Inauguration of Phase 1 of Patna 
Medical College and Hospital in 
Bihar which, upon completion, 
will become world’s second-largest 
hospital
• Achieved significant milestones at 
the Rajasthan Atomic Power Plant 
(RAPP) units 7 & 8 with the project’s 
Natural Draught Cooling Towers 
(NDCTs) and related works being 
executed ahead of schedule
• Inauguration of the south-side 
arm of Thane Creek Bridge-III in 
Maharashtra
Varanasi Cricket Stadium, Gajari, Uttar Pradesh
Group businesses

2026, your Company has now 
embarked on its next 5-year strategic 
growth plan, Lakshya 2031, to 
enhance the agility and resilience 
of its business model. The objective 
is to make the organisation more 
future-ready through accelerated 
adoption of digital technologies

improved profitability, and continued 
incubation of new-age businesses. As 
your Company continues to explore 
opportunities in emerging sectors and 
new geographies, the grooming of 
next-generation leaders capable of 
navigating the digital age is a priority. 
While some businesses of your 
Company may face temporary 
headwinds due to the ongoing 
geopolitical uncertainties, the well 
diversified portfolio of projects, 
products, services and solutions will 
ensure a steady and balanced mix of 
revenue streams.
